column2: MAE-ST dependency manifest -- target host: NVIDIA DGX Spark (spark-e269)
Tab-separated. Read and executed by conda.sh, which lives next to this file.
Lines starting with '#' are comments. Lines starting with '#!' are metadata
parsed by the script (they are NOT comments to the script).
To target a different machine: copy this file to deps.<host>.tsv, edit the
#!target line and the affected rows, then run
./conda.sh deps.<host>.tsv
No change to conda.sh should ever be needed to support a new host.
COLUMNS
stage      install order group; stages run in ascending order. Rows in
the same stage sharing installer+source+flags+required are
merged into ONE command, so co-dependent packages
(torch/torchvision) resolve together.
package    distribution name as the installer knows it
version    'latest' | exact ('0.4.5') | range ('>=2.7') | 'match-torch'
Ignored when the source names an artifact outright (direct=,
git=, local=) -- the URL already pins it.
arch       platform tag this row was VALIDATED on. Documentation, not a
filter. See WHEELS below.
installer  'conda' | 'pip'
source     where the package comes from. Grammar below.
flags      extra installer flags, '-' for none
required   'yes' aborts on failure, 'no' warns and continues
note       why this row exists / why this pin
SOURCE GRAMMAR
A ';'-separated list of scheme=value pairs. Combine freely.
pip
pypi                default index (adds nothing to the command)
index=<url>         --index-url <url>        REPLACES the default index
extra=<url>         --extra-index-url <url>  searched IN ADDITION
links=<url>         --find-links <url> -- an HTML page or directory
listing .whl files. This is how vendor repos that
are not PEP 503 indexes are consumed (NVIDIA's ARM
wheel pages, an internal LCAD server, an NFS mount).
direct=<url>        install that exact artifact. Bypasses resolution
entirely -- the URL IS the wheel.
git=<url>@<ref>     builds 'pkg @ git+<url>@<ref>'. Pin a tag or SHA,
never a branch.
local=<path>        a .whl file or a directory on this machine
conda
channel=<a>[,<b>]   -c a -c b, in the order written (order is priority).
Values may be channel names or full URLs.
nodefaults          --override-channels

column2: WHEELS -- why there is no 'wheel' column
A wheel is a prebuilt Python package: a zip named
torch-2.7.1-cp310-cp310-manylinux_2_28_aarch64.whl
name  version   py    abi      platform tag
There is one wheel per (python version x ABI x platform), NOT one per
architecture -- torch 2.7.1 ships 24 files on PyPI for exactly that reason.
Pure-Python packages ship a single 'py3-none-any' wheel (timm 0.4.5).
Packages with no wheel at all ship an sdist and are compiled at install
time (pytorchvideo 0.1.5).
pip computes this host's compatible tag set and picks the match. The wheel
is therefore an OUTPUT of resolution, not an input -- a 'wheel' column
would be recording a result as if it were a choice. What you actually pin
is version + source. To pin the exact artifact anyway, use direct=.
Version alone does not identify a binary: torch 2.7.1 from PyPI and torch
2.7.1 from download.pytorch.org/whl/cu128 are different builds against
different CUDA runtimes. The source column carries that distinction, which
is why it is not optional.
'cuda=' is the maximum runtime the DRIVER supports, as reported by
nvidia-smi -- that is what conda.sh compares against, so the two must be
the same quantity. It is NOT the installed toolkit: this host runs driver
595.71.05 (CUDA 13.2) with nvcc 13.0 in /usr/local/cuda-13.0. The
distinction does not matter for mae_st, which compiles nothing, but it
will the moment a host needs a row that builds a CUDA extension.

column9: Pinned from the lock. Needed to build any sdist with --no-build-isolation. conda-forge's python already ships this version, so pip finds it satisfied.

column2: torch
column9: Pinned from the lock and validated on this host (verify ran matmul and Conv3d on the GPU). conda pytorch-cuda does NOT exist for linux-aarch64. The '+cu128' local version AND the index are both load-bearing: torch 2.11.0 from PyPI is a different binary. Its arch_list stops at sm_120, which covers this sm_121 GB10 through CUDA minor-version binary compatibility. This row also pins the whole CUDA stack: torch declares cuda-toolkit, cudnn, nccl and friends with exact ==.

column2: torchvision
column9: Pinned from the lock; was 'match-torch'. This build requires torch==2.11.0 exactly, so the pair is self-consistent. Kept in the same command as torch so pip resolves them together. torchaudio deliberately omitted -- nothing in the repo imports it.

column2: numpy
column9: REVERSAL of a documented omission, on new evidence. util/video_vit.py:5 does 'from numpy.core.einsumfunc import _update_other_results' -- a PRIVATE numpy API. numpy 2 still serves it through a deprecation shim (verified on this exact version), but the shim will eventually go and the repo stops importing. The symbol is never used, so the clean fix is deleting that import line; until someone does, this pin is what keeps the repo importable. This is NOT the old 1.23.5 pin, which was wrong for other reasons.

column2: NOTES
[P1] pytorchvideo 0.1.5 -- a blocker, not a curiosity
The package installs without error. Importing it does not:
pytorchvideo.transforms.__init__ loads augmix -> augmentations.py,
which does `import torchvision.transforms.functional_tensor`, a module
removed in torchvision 0.17. Confirmed on this host with torchvision
util/kinetics.py:13 imports from it at MODULE TOP LEVEL, and
main_pretrain.py:31 does `from util.kinetics import Kinetics`.
Therefore `import main_pretrain` raises ModuleNotFoundError and
training cannot start at all. This fires BEFORE the three known
blockers inside main_pretrain, so it is the first thing to clear.
The five symbols taken from pytorchvideo are used only inside
Kinetics.get_pretrain_augmentation() (util/kinetics.py:447), whose one
call site is commented out at line 164. Deleting the import block at
lines 13-19 is therefore safe.
Correction to an earlier reading: the neighbouring
`torchvision.transforms._transforms_video` import at line 22 does NOT
fail. That module still exists in torchvision 0.26 and only emits a
DeprecationWarning. It needs no change.
Fixing the clone is a decision, not an install step, so this installer
deliberately does neither.
DELIBERATE OMISSIONS
numpy         NO LONGER OMITTED -- it now has a row in 30-core. The old
reasoning stands as far as it went: upstream's numpy==1.23.5
pin is wrong, the repo has no np.float / np.int / np.bool,
and torch pulls numpy>=2 regardless. What that reading
missed is util/video_vit.py:5, which imports a PRIVATE numpy
symbol still reachable only through a deprecation shim. See
the row's note. The pin is to hold that shim, not to satisfy
a version range.
detectron2    Installed by create_venv_cu128.sh, imported nowhere in the
repo. Building it from source on aarch64 is expensive and
buys nothing.
fvcore, yacs, scipy, pandas, cloudpickle, parameterized, black
Present in upstream environment.yml, unreachable from
run_pretrain.py. (fvcore/parameterized come back as
transitive deps of pytorchvideo if that row succeeds.)
youtube-dl, yt-dlp
For the ActivityNet Kinetics crawler bundled in the repo,
which downloads the public Kinetics dataset. Not needed when
the videos are produced locally, which is the case here.
torchaudio    Installed by create_venv_cu*.sh, imported nowhere.
cuda-nvcc, cuda-cudart-dev, cuda-cccl
A CUDA toolkit inside the env is needed only when something
compiles CUDA extensions at install time. mae_st has NO
compiled extensions -- it is pure Python over torch, and the
torch wheel ships its own CUDA runtime. Omitted on purpose.
A manifest for a project that DOES build extensions would
add them back as 00-env rows.
WHAT THIS FILE DOES NOT PIN
Every row above is pinned to a version measured on this host and recorded
in lock.dgx-spark.txt. That closes more than it looks: torch declares its
CUDA stack (cuda-toolkit, cudnn, nccl, cusparselt, nvshmem) with exact ==,
so pinning torch pins all of it.
What still floats is roughly twenty pure-Python transitives that nothing
here names: tensorboard's (absl-py, grpcio, markdown, protobuf, werkzeug),
matplotlib's (contourpy, fonttools, kiwisolver, cycler, pyparsing,
python-dateutil), torch's soft ones (sympy, networkx, jinja2, fsspec,
filelock, typing-extensions) and pytorchvideo's (fvcore, yacs, portalocker,
tqdm, termcolor, tabulate, parameterized).
Closing that last gap needs a constraints file rather than more rows --
pip install -c, with lock.dgx-spark.txt as the input. That is a mechanism
decision, not taken here. Naming the gap is the point: an unpinned
transitive you know about is a risk; one you have not noticed is a bug
waiting to be blamed on something else.
